question: What does the most recent news article on proteinatlas.org report: which journal was the study published in, who led the team, and what did they identify?

turns.text: I'll start by finding the news section on proteinatlas.org.
Let me look at the most recent news articles. I'll open the top ones listed.
The pages have a lot of navigation boilerplate before the article content. Let me read the actual article text by fetching further into each page.

The 2026-09-10 article is an "Image of the Week," and the 2026-08-27 one is a "Publication" report. Let me check the full 2026 listing and the other recent publication articles to find the most recent one that reports a study.
Let me examine the main news listing more closely to confirm the ordering and check for any featured article.
The press room confirms the news article ordering. Let me read the second-most-recent article (the 2026-09-02 Q&A) and the August listing to be thorough.

I now have what I need. Here's what the recent news pages show.

## Findings

**Which article is "most recent"?** On the news index the newest items are:
- 2026-09-10 — "Multiplex tissue image of the month – PDX1 in pancreas" — this is only an *"Image of the Week / Image of the month"* post (an mIHC image of PDX1), not a report of a study (source: https://www.proteinatlas.org/news/2026-09-10/multiplex-tissue-image-of-the-month-pdx1-in-pancreas).
- 2026-09-02 — "Reducing uncertainty in drug development: a Q&A with Thomas Helleday" — this is the most recent news article that actually *reports a study* (and it hangs on the news index right below the image post: https://www.proteinatlas.org/news).

**What that most recent study-reporting article says** — "Reducing uncertainty in drug development: a Q&A with Thomas Helleday" (dated 2026-09-02):

- **Journal:** *Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy* ("In a recent study published in Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy…").
- **Who led the team:** Thomas Helleday and Theodora Manolakou ("a team led by Thomas Helleday and Theodora Manolakou").
- **What they identified:** "a novel, targetable transcriptional-metabolic axis that sustains inflammatory T-cell responses" — specifically MTHFD1/MTHFD2-dependent one-carbon metabolism in pathogenic inflammatory T cells, relevant to rheumatoid arthritis (and pursued via the compound TH9619 / One-Carbon Therapeutics).

Source: https://www.proteinatlas.org/news/2026-09-02/reducing-uncertainty-in-drug-development-a-q-a-with-thomas-helleday

## Caveats (stated plainly)
- The single **newest** item on the news page (2026-09-10) is an "*Image of the Week*" (PDX1 in pancreas) and does **not** report a study published in a journal, so it does **not** answer the journal/team/finding parts of the question (https://www.proteinatlas.org/news/2026-09-10/multiplex-tissue-image-of-the-month-pdx1-in-pancreas).
- The most recent item tagged in the "**Publication**" category is the 2026-08-27 piece on the HPA Multiplex tissue resource, published in *Protein Science*; that article does **not** name a team leader (https://www.proteinatlas.org/news/2026-08-27/the-multiplex-tissue-resource-provides-deeper-spatial-insight-into-protein-expression).

## Final answer
The most recent news article that reports a study — the 2026-09-02 Q&A with Thomas Helleday — states the work was **published in *Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy***, was **led by Thomas Helleday and Theodora Manolakou**, and that the team **identified a novel, targetable transcriptional-metabolic axis that sustains inflammatory T-cell responses** (MTHFD1/MTHFD2 one-carbon metabolism, relevant to rheumatoid arthritis). (Only the 2026-09-10 "image of the month" post is newer, and it is not a study report.)
